Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Baltimore MD/Washington DC
851 PM EDT Sat Sep 5 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
No major changes were made to the latest forecast package.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
- 1) Isolated showers linger through the evening, but there will
  be no severe weather threat.

- 2) Drier conditions with seasonable temperatures and lower 
  humidity Sunday into early next week.

- 3) Shower and thunderstorm chances return by mid week.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
KEY MESSAGE 1...Isolated showers linger through the evening, but
there will be no severe weather threat. 

The primary cold front is currently nosing southward while
moving into northern sections of North Carolina. Despite the
post-frontal air mass, humidity levels have not fully dropped
off yet with current dew points in the mid 60s to low 70s.
Compared the 00Z IAD sounding from the one this morning showed
much of the drying occurring in the 700-mb and above layer. Looking
on radar, most afternoon activity has waned with the loss of 
daytime heating. However, some residual isolated showers 
persist, mainly along I-64 and up toward the Shenandoah Valley. 
These too should dissipate in time with diminishing levels of 
instability. Low temperatures will drop several degrees from 
previous nights into the 60s for most, even mid 50s in the 
mountains.


KEY MESSAGE 2...Drier conditions with seasonable temperatures and 
lower humidity Sunday into early next week.

Broad high pressure over the Great Lakes will track over the 
Mid-Atlantic Sunday into Monday, with accompanying mid-level 
dry air that will bring down humidity and t-storm chances. Daily
highs drop into the low 80s, along with drier dewpoints in the 
mid to upper 50s. Overnight lows in the 50s and low 60s.

Surface high pressure begins to transition south of the Mid-Atlantic 
on Tuesday as upper level ridging builds over the Southeast. 
Temperatures likely begin to creep up again during this time, 
accompanied by increasing humidity as mid-level dry air tracks south 
of the region with more humid air coming in from the north. This 
will correspond with strong upper-level trough forming over Quebec 
around midweek, with an accompanying cold front tracking across the 
East Coast sometime between Wednesday and Thursday. This could 
create some chances for precipitation over the region, with some 
indicators for low-end instability over the area as this mid-level 
moisture tracks southeast. Severe probabilities look low at this 
time, but a few thunderstorms are not completely out of the question 
as this front moves through.

Looking towards late next week, temperatures likely drop again in 
the wake of this cold front Friday as it tracks to the south.


KEY MESSAGE 3...Shower and thunderstorm chances return by mid
week.

Entering into the later half of next week, southerly return flow 
from a high pressure system just off the Mid-Atlatic coast drives 
warm, moist air into our region. Models depict a surface low 
deepening over Quebec and advancing a corresponding cold front 
through our region sometime late next week. There is still a quite a 
bit of uncertainty associated with the arrival of this boundary to 
our region, with its arrival ranging between Wednesday and Thursday. 
A bove-normal high temperatures and dew points out ahead of this 
boundary could potentially destabilize the atmosphere and lead to 
showers and thunderstorms late next week.

&&

.AVIATION /00Z SUNDAY THROUGH THURSDAY/...
A few showers may linger into the night at KCHO, but these will
be more or less off and on. 

VFR conditions should persist Sunday through Wednesday evening.
Flight categories could deteriorate with showers and 
thunderstorms returning on Thursday. Light southerly winds on 
Wednesday shift northwesterly and strengthen by Thursday.

&&

.MARINE...
No marine hazards are expected through the holiday weekend. 
Generally light flow is expected, though onshore gusts could 
approach marginal SCA levels late Sunday afternoon.

Northeasterly winds Monday shift southerly on Tuesday. Winds 
stay below 15 knots through Monday and Tuesday. Winds could 
increase to SCA levels on Wednesday into Thursday ahead of an 
incoming cold front.

&&

.TIDES/COASTAL FLOODING...
Tidal anomalies remain elevated over the next several days due
to an onshore flow. Minor tidal flooding is possible at
Annapolis, and could also be possible in the other sensitive
tidal locations in the northern Chesapeake Bay.
